notes: Write your own plain-English summaries; do not copy the official descriptors verbatim.

items.name: Listening
items.intro: Listening has 40 questions, one mark each. Your raw score is converted to a band. Academic and General Training use the same test and the same scale.

items.label: Part 1
items.title: Everyday conversation
items.text: Two people in a social situation, e.g. booking or registering. Easiest part.

items.label: Part 2
items.title: Everyday monologue
items.text: One speaker on a social topic, e.g. a guided tour or announcement.

items.label: Part 3
items.title: Study conversation
items.text: Up to four people in an educational or training context, e.g. students and a tutor.

items.label: Part 4
items.title: Academic lecture
items.text: One speaker on an academic subject. Hardest part.

blocks.title: Raw score to band
blocks.note: Approximate: the official conversion shifts slightly from test to test. The app uses this table for your practice scores.

blocks.title: What Listening tests
items: Opinions, attitudes and a speaker's purpose
Recognising paraphrase: the question rarely uses the speaker's words
Telling apart similar-sounding information and corrections

blocks.title: How answers are marked
items: No penalty for wrong answers, so never leave a blank.
Spelling must be correct; a missing plural -s can make an answer wrong.
Going over the word limit (e.g. NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) makes the answer wrong.
Paper test: 10 minutes to transfer answers. Computer test: 2 minutes to check.
